<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">

# cyclonedx-to-openvex

<a href="#cyclonedx-to-openvex" id="user-content-cyclonedx-to-openvex" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: cyclonedx-to-openvex"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="octicon octicon-link" /></a>

</div>

<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/getreeldev/cyclonedx-to-openvex" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/5d31d24852b5d75789981955a597dd39cc4591c7f1d74bb6f9ea678978fca9f1/68747470733a2f2f706b672e676f2e6465762f62616467652f6769746875622e636f6d2f6765747265656c6465762f6379636c6f6e6564782d746f2d6f70656e7665782e737667" style="max-width: 100%;" data-canonical-src="https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/getreeldev/cyclonedx-to-openvex.svg" alt="Go Reference" /></a>

Go library + CLI that converts a CycloneDX BOM's embedded VEX (`vulnerabilities[].analysis`) into an <a href="https://openvex.dev" rel="nofollow">OpenVEX</a> 0.2.0 document. Zero dependencies beyond the standard library.

The two formats use incompatible status/justification vocabularies, and CycloneDX is finer-grained than OpenVEX — so the conversion is deterministic but **lossy** in places. This library makes the loss explicit rather than hiding it:

- the mapping is a published, versioned spec file — [`crosswalk/crosswalk.yaml`](/getreeldev/cyclonedx-to-openvex/blob/main/crosswalk/crosswalk.yaml) — with a **fidelity** flag (`exact` / `lossy` / `contested`) on every entry;
- every converted statement records its provenance in `status_notes`;
- `-reject-lossy` skips anything that isn't an exact mapping, for strict OpenVEX.

See [`docs/crosswalk.md`](/getreeldev/cyclonedx-to-openvex/blob/main/docs/crosswalk.md) for the mapping model, fidelity, direction, and how the spec file is maintained.

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">

## Install

<a href="#install" id="user-content-install" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Install"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="octicon octicon-link" /></a>

</div>

<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="go get github.com/getreeldev/cyclonedx-to-openvex">

    go get github.com/getreeldev/cyclonedx-to-openvex

</div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">

## Use

<a href="#use" id="user-content-use" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Use"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="octicon octicon-link" /></a>

</div>

Library:

<div class="highlight highlight-source-go notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="import &quot;github.com/getreeldev/cyclonedx-to-openvex/translator&quot;

// r is any io.Reader of a CycloneDX BOM. report lists every mapping and skip.
doc, report, err := translator.FromCycloneDX(r, translator.Options{})">

    import "github.com/getreeldev/cyclonedx-to-openvex/translator"

    // r is any io.Reader of a CycloneDX BOM. report lists every mapping and skip.
    doc, report, err := translator.FromCycloneDX(r, translator.Options{})

</div>

CLI:

<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="cyclonedx-to-openvex &lt; bom.cdx.json &gt; out.openvex.json   # convert
cyclonedx-to-openvex -report &lt; bom.cdx.json &gt; out.json   # + report on stderr
cyclonedx-to-openvex -reject-lossy &lt; bom.cdx.json        # strict: skip non-exact mappings">

    cyclonedx-to-openvex < bom.cdx.json > out.openvex.json   # convert
    cyclonedx-to-openvex -report < bom.cdx.json > out.json   # + report on stderr
    cyclonedx-to-openvex -reject-lossy < bom.cdx.json        # strict: skip non-exact mappings

</div>

A `not_affected` carrying a CycloneDX justification, converted (note the preserved provenance):

<div class="highlight highlight-source-json-comments notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" snippet-clipboard-copy-content="// in:  state=not_affected, justification=requires_environment
{
  &quot;vulnerability&quot;: { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;CVE-2022-42898&quot; },
  &quot;products&quot;: [ { &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;pkg:deb/debian/libk5crypto3@1.18.3-6%2Bdeb11u2?arch=amd64&amp;distro=debian-11.5&quot; } ],
  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;not_affected&quot;,
  &quot;justification&quot;: &quot;vulnerable_code_cannot_be_controlled_by_adversary&quot;,
  &quot;status_notes&quot;: &quot;converted_from=cyclonedx-vex; original_state=not_affected; original_justification=requires_environment; fidelity=lossy&quot;
}">

    // in:  state=not_affected, justification=requires_environment
    {
      "vulnerability": { "name": "CVE-2022-42898" },
      "products": [ { "@id": "pkg:deb/debian/libk5crypto3@1.18.3-6%2Bdeb11u2?arch=amd64&distro=debian-11.5" } ],
      "status": "not_affected",
      "justification": "vulnerable_code_cannot_be_controlled_by_adversary",
      "status_notes": "converted_from=cyclonedx-vex; original_state=not_affected; original_justification=requires_environment; fidelity=lossy"
    }

</div>

`requires_environment` has no exact OpenVEX equivalent, so it collapses to the nearest CISA bucket, flagged `lossy`, with the original kept in `status_notes`.
